3	- **Code quality:** error handling (swallowed exceptions, overly broad catch, missing handling, async errors); performance (N+1 queries, CPU-intensive ops in hot paths, missing cache, unbounded memory); boundary conditions (null/undefined, empty collections, numeric boundaries, off-by-one). Flag issues that may cause silent failures or production incidents.
4	- **Removal candidates:** propose deletion only when a demonstrated current cost or defect justifies it and required behavior is preserved. A pending task's unreachable scaffold or disabled feature is not, by itself, a removal candidate. Distinguish **safe delete now** vs **defer with plan** when removal is warranted.
5	
6	### 7) Self-check and confidence assessment
7	
8	For **each finding** from Steps 5–6:
9	
10	1. Re-read the relevant code and surrounding context independently.
11	2. Ask: **"Could I be misreading the code?"** — trace execution paths, check for runtime behavior, configuration, or framework conventions that might make this correct.
12	3. Ask: **"Is this a real issue or a style preference?"** — distinguish between bugs/risks and subjective choices that don't affect correctness or security.
13	4. Ask: **"What's the actual impact?"** — verify that the severity matches the real-world consequence, not just the theoretical violation.
14	5. Assign final confidence score (1–100%) with **explicit reasoning** documenting:
15	   - What was verified
16	   - What evidence supports the finding
17	   - What uncertainty remains
18	6. Downgrade or **remove** findings that don't survive the self-check.
19	
20	### 8) Index findings
21	
22	Index any P0/P1 findings that suggest a systemic or structural pattern (not isolated typos or one-off mistakes) as `kk:review-findings`. Index on first encounter — recurrence detection happens on the search side in future reviews.
23	
24	- If no P0/P1 systemic findings exist, explicitly note "No findings to index" and move on.
25	- This step is mandatory — do not skip it even if the review found no issues.
26	
27	### 9) Present results
28	
29	#### Output format
30	
31	Structure your review as follows:
32	
33	```markdown
34	## Code Review Summary
35	
36	**Files reviewed**: X files, Y lines changed
37	**Overall assessment**: [APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT]
38	**Intent and scope**: requirement source, current task/request, selected diff and candidate state
39	**Baselines**: review base/candidate; separate release baseline if applicable
40	
41	## Behavior and Compatibility
42	
43	Inspected paths/scenarios, observed results and evidence limits. Include applicable
44	Supported / Blocked / Unknown / Not applicable conclusions with named baselines.
45	Attribute author-supplied results and inherited issues. Record outstanding evidence
46	or release prerequisites, next actions and durable tracking locations when deferred.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Findings
51	
52	### P0 - Critical
53	
54	(none or list)
55	
56	### P1 - High
57	
58	- **[file:line]** Brief title
59	  - Profile: {profile_name} · Checklist: {checklist_filename}
60	  - Triggered by: {signal_type} — {signal_description}
61	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
62	  - Confidence: 90% - reasoning behind the confidence level
63	  - Suggested fix
64	
65	- **[another_file:line]** Brief title
66	  - Profile: generic · Checklist: —
67	  - Triggered by: —
68	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
69	  - Confidence: 60% - reasoning behind the confidence level
70	  - Suggested fix
71	
72	### P2 - Medium
73	
74	...
75	
76	### P3 - Low
77	
78	...
79	
80	---
81	
82	## Removal/Iteration Plan
83	
84	(if applicable)
85	
86	Only include recommendations tied to a demonstrated issue or an identified,
87	currently required verification gap. A clean scoped review needs no extra work.
88	```
89	
90	**Inline comments**: Use this format for file-specific findings:
91	
92	```
93	::code-comment{file="path/to/file" line="42" severity="P1"}
94	Description of the issue and suggested fix.
95	::
96	```
97	
98	Apply [functional-review.md](functional-review.md)'s verdict mapping: a hard acceptance/delivery violation cannot be approved; material Unknown evidence receives COMMENT absent a demonstrated blocker. Out-of-scope operational unknowns do not automatically downgrade an explicitly scoped code verdict. Preserve P0–P3 impact severity and distinguish code correctness from release readiness.
99	
100	**Every review** reports coverage and limits, even with findings. When no issues are found, explicitly state:
101	
102	- What was checked
103	- Any areas not covered (e.g., "Did not verify database migrations")
104	- Specific residual risks or required verification gaps, when supported
105	
106	### 10) Next steps confirmation
107	
108	After presenting findings, ask user how to proceed:
109	
110	```markdown
111	---
112	
113	## Next Steps
114	
115	I found X issues (P0: ..., P1: ..., P2: ..., P3: ...).
116	
117	The actionable items I recommend fixing:
118	1. P1 ...
119	2. P2 ...
120	3. P3 ...
121	
122	Items I recommend keeping as is:
123	- ...: the finding is a false-positive because ...
124	- ...: correct behavior because ...
125	- ...: mirrors production behavior of ...
126	
127	**How would you like to proceed?**
128	
129	1. **Fix all** - I'll implement all suggested fixes
130	2. **Fix P0/P1 only** - Address critical and high priority issues
131	3. **Fix specific items** - Tell me which issues to fix
132	4. **No changes** - Review complete, no implementation needed
133	
134	Please choose an option or provide specific instructions.
135	```
136	
137	**Important**: Do NOT implement any changes until user explicitly confirms. This is a review-first workflow.
138	
139	### 11) Verify outputs
140	
141	Before declaring the review complete, check each item in the **Required Outputs** section of SKILL.md:
142	
143	- [ ] Review report presented to user
144	- [ ] Intent, scope/baselines, inspected behavior, applicable compatibility conclusions and evidence limits reported
145	- [ ] P0/P1 systemic findings indexed as `kk:review-findings` (or explicitly noted "No findings to index")
146	- [ ] Next steps confirmation from user
147	
148	If any item is unchecked, go back and complete it before proceeding.
149	
150	END SOURCE

156	# Capy Knowledge Base Protocol
157	
158	If `capy` MCP tools are not available in this session, skip all search and index steps below and proceed normally.
159	
160	## Source Label Taxonomy
161	
162	All plugin-managed labels use the `kk:` namespace prefix.
163	
164	| Label                    | Contents                                                              |
165	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
166	| `kk:arch-decisions`      | Architecture decisions, design rationale, trade-offs                  |
167	| `kk:review-findings`     | Code review patterns, recurring issues, anti-patterns                 |
168	| `kk:lang-idioms`         | Language best practices, idiomatic patterns from external sources     |
169	| `kk:project-conventions` | Discovered project patterns, naming conventions, structural decisions |
170	| `kk:test-patterns`       | Testing approaches, edge cases, test infrastructure decisions         |
171	| `kk:debug-context`       | Root causes, tricky bugs and their fixes, environment gotchas         |
172	
173	## Search Conventions
174	
175	- Use 2-4 specific terms per query — not vague keywords
176	- Always scope with `source` filter to relevant `kk:*` labels
177	- Use `source: "kk:"` only for broad cross-domain searches (e.g., CoVe verification)
178	- Default `limit: 3` per query unless more context is needed
179	- **Cold-start fallback:** If no results, proceed with standard guidelines — empty results are normal for new projects
180	
181	## Index Conventions
182	
183	- Only index non-obvious learnings not derivable from reading the code or git history
184	- Keep content concise — summarize the insight, don't dump raw output
185	- Always use a `kk:` prefixed label from the taxonomy above
186	- One concept per `capy_index` call — don't bundle unrelated learnings
187	- Skip indexing if the insight is already captured in design docs or CLAUDE.md
188	
189	END SOURCE

195	## Profile detection procedure
196	
197	Single source of truth for computing the set of profiles active in the current context.
198	Consumed by six skills: `/kk:review-code`, `/kk:review-spec`, `/kk:design`, `/kk:implement`, `/kk:test`, and `/kk:document`.
199	
200	Every profile under `klaude-plugin/profiles/<name>/` declares its own trigger rule in `DETECTION.md` using the mandatory three-section schema (`## Path signals`, `## Filename signals`, `## Content signals`).
201	The shared procedure below applies the same algorithm against every profile's declared values.
202	
203	### Inputs per consuming skill
204	
205	Not every consumer has a diff available. Use the input listed for your skill:
206	
207	- **`/kk:review-code`** — git diff (staged, or an explicit commit range). Scope is
208	  the set of files the diff touches.
209	- **`/kk:review-spec`** — git diff when invoked standalone; the feature directory's
210	  full file list when invoked by `/kk:implement` (spec review runs over the whole
211	  feature, not just the current task's diff).
212	- **`/kk:test`** — git diff mid-feature, OR the feature directory's file list
213	  post-implementation.
214	- **`/kk:implement`** — the current sub-task's target file list, augmented by the
215	  diff accumulated so far in the feature.
216	- **`/kk:design`** — **no file list available** (implementation does not yet exist).
217	  Detection uses a user-declared or keyword-inferred signal instead; see
218	  [The `/kk:design` interaction pattern](#the-design-interaction-pattern) below.
219	- **`/kk:document`** — feature directory's current file list; diff optional.
220	
221	### The `/kk:design` interaction pattern
222	
223	The design phase runs before any code exists, so file-based detection is impossible. Detection uses idea-prose keyword matching against tokens declared in each profile's `DETECTION.md`.
224	
225	**Algorithm:**
226	
227	1. **Collect tokens.** Iterate §Known profiles. For each `<name>`, `Read` `${TOOLBOX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/profiles/<name>/DETECTION.md`. If the file has no `## Design signals` section, skip — that profile does not participate in design-phase detection. Otherwise, parse `display_name` and `tokens` from the section.
228	2. **Build union.** Collect all declared tokens into a single set, each tagged by its source profile name and `display_name`.
229	3. **Match.** Check the idea prose against the union. Matching is case-insensitive, whole-word (so `pod` in "podcast" does not fire).
230	4. **Confirm.** On match, surface a confirmation prompt per matched profile:
231	   *"This appears to be a {display_name} feature. Activate the {profile_name} profile?"* — let the user confirm yes/no. When multiple profiles match, confirm each independently.
232	5. **Fallback.** If no token matches but the idea is **ambiguous** — names infrastructure, deployment, runtime, or platform concerns without naming a specific technology (e.g., _"add a caching layer for the service"_, _"build a CI pipeline"_, _"deploy to production"_); or includes overloaded tokens that collide across domains — build the fallback prompt dynamically from all profiles that declare `## Design signals`:
233	   *"Does this feature involve {display_name_1, display_name_2, ...}? If yes, which?"*
234	
235	Confirmation is required — the /kk:design skill never auto-activates a profile silently. The narrow per-profile token sets avoid noisy false positives from tokens that overload across domains.
236	
237	Once activated, subsequent design-phase steps treat the profile as active in the same record shape produced by file-based detection (see §Output shape).
238	
239	### Known profiles
240	
241	This is the authoritative enumeration of profile `<name>`s — do NOT try discover profiles via any other means.
242	An explicit list is boring, deterministic, and unambiguous; runtime filesystem enumeration against the plugin tree has proven unreliable.
243	
244	- `go`
245	- `python`
246	- `java`
247	- `js_ts`
248	
249	END PACKET PART 2/6
